definitions.gloss: every other ~; at intervals of ~; leaving a gap of ~
definitions.explanation: Attaches to a number-plus-counter phrase to state the size of the gap between one occurrence and the next. Because it names the gap rather than the cycle, {一日|いちにち}おきに means every second day, not every day. Used for gaps in time and in space alike.

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}は{一日|いちにち}おきに{飲|の}んでください。
examples.english: Please take the medicine every other day.

examples.japanese: この{駅|えき}からは{十五分|じゅうごふん}おきにバスが{出|で}ている。
examples.english: Buses leave this station every fifteen minutes.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}の{両側|りょうがわ}に{十|じゅう}メートルおきに{桜|さくら}の{木|き}が{植|う}えられている。
examples.english: Cherry trees are planted at ten-meter intervals along both sides of the road.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{様子|ようす}が{心配|しんぱい}なので、{二日|ふつか}おきに{電話|でんわ}をかけるようにしている。
examples.english: I'm worried about how my grandmother is doing, so I make a point of phoning every third day.

notes:
From {置|お}く (to place, to leave), so the literal sense is "leaving ~ in between."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一日|いちにち}おきに: every other day (one day skipped)
- {一週間|いっしゅうかん}おきに: every two weeks
- {一行|いちぎょう}おきに: on every other line
- {一|ひと}つおきに: every other one
- {三十分|さんじゅっぷん}おきに: every thirty minutes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ごとに: every ~ — counts the unit itself, so {一日|いちにち}ごとに is every single day, while {一日|いちにち}おきに is every second day. With durations such as {三十分|さんじゅっぷん}, the two come out the same, and speakers often use them interchangeably there.

COMMON MISTAKES:
With counters of two or more, native usage is not fully consistent; {二日|ふつか}おきに is normally every third day, but some speakers say it for every second day. When precision matters, say {三日|みっか}に{一度|いちど} (once every three days) instead.
